![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224989/assets/751d38a1a37afd277cbd54850abf61db898a231b49ad0d4bcaa5964bbab601e1.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{4}{5},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta .$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224989/assets/0534847b2363ff75e053b9d05736ff367f2ad6da527b7100de0018d003c4c9df.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{4}{5}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{4}{5}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{4}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{16}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{9}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{3}{5}.$

Finally, knowing that $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(\frac{3}{5})}=\frac{5}{3}.
$$
